nodes.title: Pitch and Sound Frequency
nodes.description: The highness or lowness of a sound determined by frequency; notated vertically on the staff.

nodes.title: The Musical Staff & Ledger Lines
nodes.description: Five lines and four spaces that provide reference for pitch height, extended by ledger lines.

nodes.title: Treble Clef (G Clef)
nodes.description: Designates the second line from bottom as G4; used for soprano, violin, flute, piano right hand.

nodes.title: Bass Clef (F Clef)
nodes.description: Designates the fourth line from bottom as F3; used for bass, cello, trombone, piano left hand.

nodes.title: The Grand Staff and Middle C
nodes.description: Combining treble and bass staves joined by a brace, centered around Middle C (C4).

nodes.title: Half Steps, Whole Steps, and Accidentals
nodes.description: The smallest intervals in Western music; sharps, flats, and naturals.

nodes.title: American Standard Pitch Notation (ASPN)
nodes.description: Scientific pitch designation combining letter name and octave number (e.g. C4 = Middle C).

nodes.title: Rhythmic and Rest Values
nodes.description: Whole, half, quarter, eighth, and sixteenth notes and rests; ties and beams.

nodes.title: Simple Meter and Time Signatures
nodes.description: Time signatures where each beat divides into two equal parts (2/4, 3/4, 4/4).

nodes.title: Compound Meter and Time Signatures
nodes.description: Time signatures where each beat divides into three equal parts (6/8, 9/8, 12/8).

nodes.title: Major Scales and Key Signatures
nodes.description: Diatonic scale with step pattern W-W-H-W-W-W-H; key signatures and Circle of Fifths.

nodes.title: Minor Scales (Natural, Harmonic, Melodic)
nodes.description: Natural minor step pattern W-H-W-W-H-W-W, plus harmonic (raised 7) and melodic forms.

nodes.title: Diatonic and Chromatic Intervals
nodes.description: Distance between two pitches; generic size (2nd, 3rd...) and quality (Major, Minor, Perfect...).

nodes.title: Triads (Major, Minor, Diminished, Augmented)
nodes.description: Three-note chords stacked in thirds: root, third, and fifth.

nodes.title: Seventh Chords
nodes.description: Four-note chords: Major 7th, Dominant 7th, Minor 7th, Half-Diminished, and Fully Diminished.

nodes.title: Inversion and Figured Bass
nodes.description: Root position, 1st inversion (6), 2nd inversion (6/4); Baroque basso continuo figures.

nodes.title: Roman Numerals and SATB Voice Leading
nodes.description: Harmonic analysis using Roman numerals (I, IV, V, vi) and four-voice choral texture.

nodes.title: \relative c' Mode
nodes.description: Concise pitch entry where each note finds the nearest octave to the previous note.

nodes.title: is / es Accidental Suffixes
nodes.description: Appending 'is' for sharps and 'es' for flats.

nodes.title: \clef Command
nodes.description: Sets the staff clef to treble, bass, alto, or tenor.

nodes.title: PianoStaff Context
nodes.description: Grand Staff layout with brace combining treble and bass staves.

nodes.title: Duration Numbers & Dots
nodes.pattern: c1 c2 c4 c8 c4. r4
nodes.description: Reciprocal numbers 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 for rhythms, dot for dotted notes, r for rests.

nodes.title: \time Command
nodes.description: Defines time signature and automatic beaming.

nodes.title: \key Command
nodes.description: Sets key signature accidentals on the staff.

nodes.title: Chord Angle Brackets < >
nodes.description: Simultaneous notes enclosed in angle brackets with duration after.

nodes.title: \figures Context
nodes.description: Engraving figured bass numerals below bass staff.

nodes.title: Voice Separation << \\ >>
nodes.description: Multiple independent voices with automatic stem directions on one staff.

curriculum.title: Part I: Fundamentals of Music Theory & LilyPond Notation

lessons.title: 1. Introduction to Musical Notation & LilyPond
lessons.theory_summary: Music notation maps pitch vertically and rhythm horizontally. In LilyPond, we write code to engrave sheet music.

theory_quiz.question: In Western music notation, how is pitch represented on the staff?
options: Vertically (higher notes placed higher on staff)
theory_quiz.explanation: Pitches are positioned vertically on lines and spaces: higher frequencies sit higher on the staff.

coding_challenge.prompt: Write your first LilyPond score! Engrave four quarter notes: C, D, E, F in treble clef using \relative c'.
coding_challenge.hint: In \relative c', type: c4 d e f. Quarter notes after c4 inherit the duration 4.

lessons.title: 2. Notes, Clefs, and Ledger Lines
lessons.theory_summary: Notes consist of noteheads, stems, and flags/beams. Stems point down above the middle line, up below it. Clefs assign pitch letters to lines.

theory_quiz.question: For a note placed on or above the middle line of a staff, which direction should the stem typically point?
options: Downward (on the left side of notehead)
Upward (on the right side of notehead)
theory_quiz.explanation: Standard engraving practice points stems downward for notes above the middle line to keep stems within the staff boundaries.

coding_challenge.prompt: Engrave an ascending scale fragment from middle C (C4) to G4 in treble clef: c4 d e f g1.
coding_challenge.hint: Set \clef treble and write: c4 d e f | g1 |

lessons.title: 3. Reading Treble and Bass Clefs
lessons.theory_summary: The Treble Clef circles G4 on the 2nd line. The Bass Clef centers two dots around F3 on the 4th line.

theory_quiz.question: Which pitch does the Bass Clef specify on its fourth line (from the bottom)?
theory_quiz.explanation: The bass clef is also known as the F clef because its two dots surround the line for F3.

coding_challenge.prompt: Switch from treble clef to bass clef! Engrave C4 in treble, then switch to bass clef and engrave C3.

lessons.title: 4. The Keyboard and the Grand Staff
lessons.theory_summary: The Grand Staff unites Treble and Bass staves. Middle C (C4) sits on the ledger line directly between them.

theory_quiz.question: Where does Middle C (C4) sit on the Grand Staff?
options: On a ledger line between the treble and bass staves
On the top line of the treble staff
On the bottom line of the bass staff
On space 3 of the bass staff
theory_quiz.explanation: Middle C is one ledger line below the treble staff and one ledger line above the bass staff.

coding_challenge.prompt: Create a Piano Grand Staff! The upper staff plays G4 whole note in treble, and the lower staff plays C3 whole note in bass.
coding_challenge.hint: In the lower Staff, write: \clef bass c1

lessons.title: 5. Half Steps, Whole Steps, and Accidentals
lessons.theory_summary: A half step is the distance between two adjacent keys on a piano. Sharps raise pitch by a half step; flats lower pitch by a half step.

theory_quiz.question: How do you write an F-sharp in LilyPond?
theory_quiz.explanation: In LilyPond's Dutch naming, sharps are indicated by the suffix 'is', so F-sharp is 'fis'.

coding_challenge.prompt: Engrave C, C-sharp, D, E-flat, and E natural: c4 cis d ees e1 in \relative c'.
coding_challenge.hint: Write: c4 cis d ees | e1 |

lessons.title: 8. Rhythmic Durations, Rests, and Ties
lessons.theory_summary: Each note duration is twice as long as the next smaller value (whole = 2 halves = 4 quarters = 8 eighths). A dot adds 50% more duration.

theory_quiz.question: How many eighth notes are equal in duration to a dotted quarter note?
theory_quiz.explanation: A quarter note = 2 eighths. The dot adds half its value (1 eighth), totaling 3 eighth notes.

coding_challenge.prompt: Engrave a dotted rhythm: dotted quarter note, eighth note, followed by a half rest: c'4. d'8 r2.

lessons.title: 9. Simple Meter and Time Signatures
lessons.theory_summary: In simple meters (2/4, 3/4, 4/4), the top number indicates beats per measure, and the bottom number indicates the note value of each beat.

theory_quiz.question: In 3/4 time, how many quarter-note beats are in each measure?
theory_quiz.explanation: The top number 3 designates 3 beats per measure; the bottom number 4 designates the quarter note as the beat unit.

coding_challenge.prompt: Set \time 3/4 and engrave two measures of a waltz: measure 1 = c4 d e, measure 2 = f2.
coding_challenge.solution_code:
\version "2.24.0"
\relative c' {
  \clef treble
  \time 3/4
  c4 d e |
  f2. |
}
coding_challenge.hint: Write \time 3/4, then c4 d e | f2. |

lessons.title: 12. Major Scales and Key Signatures
lessons.theory_summary: The Major Scale follows the step pattern: Whole, Whole, Half, Whole, Whole, Whole, Half (W-W-H-W-W-W-H).

theory_quiz.question: Which accidental is found in the key signature of G major?
theory_quiz.explanation: G major has one sharp: F-sharp (fis in LilyPond).

coding_challenge.prompt: Set \key g \major and engrave the G major scale: g4 a b c | d e fis g |.
coding_challenge.solution_code:
\version "2.24.0"
\relative c' {
  \clef treble
  \key g \major
  \time 4/4
  g4 a b c |
  d4 e fis g |
}
coding_challenge.hint: Use \key g \major and remember F-sharp is written as fis.

lessons.title: 16. Intervals (Harmonic & Melodic)
lessons.theory_summary: An interval is the distance between two notes. Melodic intervals sound in sequence; harmonic intervals sound simultaneously.

theory_quiz.question: What is the interval between C4 and G4?
theory_quiz.explanation: C to G spans five letter names (C-D-E-F-G) and contains 7 half steps, forming a Perfect Fifth.

coding_challenge.prompt: Engrave three harmonic intervals in \relative c': a Major Third <c e>2, followed by a Perfect Fifth <c g>2.

lessons.title: 17. Triads (Major and Minor)
lessons.theory_summary: A triad consists of a Root, Third, and Fifth. Major triad = M3 + m3 (e.g. C-E-G). Minor triad = m3 + M3 (e.g. C-E♭-G).

theory_quiz.question: What pitches make up a C minor triad in root position?
theory_quiz.explanation: A minor triad has a minor third (C to E♭ = 3 half steps) and a perfect fifth (C to G = 7 half steps).

coding_challenge.prompt: Engrave a C major triad <c e g>2 followed by a C minor triad <c ees g>2.

lessons.title: 19. Inversions and Figured Bass
lessons.theory_summary: When the third is in the bass, the chord is in First Inversion (6). When the fifth is in the bass, it is in Second Inversion (6/4).

theory_quiz.question: In figured bass, what does the figure '6' indicate below a bass note?
options: First inversion triad (third is in the bass)
Second inversion triad (fifth is in the bass)
theory_quiz.explanation: The figure 6 is shorthand for 6/3, indicating a triad in first inversion.

coding_challenge.prompt: Engrave a bass staff with a first inversion figure: bass note e2 with figure <6>.

lessons.title: 20. Roman Numerals and SATB Voice Leading
lessons.theory_summary: Roman numerals analyze harmonic function (I = Tonic, IV = Subdominant, V = Dominant). SATB distributes harmony across Soprano, Alto, Tenor, and Bass.

theory_quiz.question: In the key of C major, which chord is the Dominant (V)?
theory_quiz.explanation: Scale degree 5 in C major is G, making G major the Dominant (V) chord.

coding_challenge.prompt: Engrave a two-voice cadence on one staff using << \\ >>: Soprano sings d4 c2, Alto sings b4 c2 in treble.
coding_challenge.hint: In the second voice, write: { b4 c2 }
